title: Around 14 GW of irregular distributed solar threatens grid security in Brazil, warns TÜV Rheinland
content:
Unauthorized distributed-generation expansions in Brazil could add up to 14 GW of unregistered capacity, complicating grid planning and operation, TÜV Rheinland warns. The expansion of PV systems up to 5 MW without proper design reviews or approvals also raises electrical safety risks and compliance concerns.

title: Colombia: Earthquake affects power grid, but no damage reported at solar plants
content:
A magnitude-7.4 earthquake in Colombia disrupted electricity supplies, leaving up to 20% of demand unmet in some affected regions. No damage has been reported at utility-scale solar plants, with the main impacts concentrated on transmission and distribution infrastructure.

title: US eases transport rules for portable lithium batteries, raising limits and cutting regulation
content:
The shift to battery-powered tools and portable power stations in the trades has been hampered by hazardous materials regulations set before the battery revolution. A new US ruling better clears the way for the portable storage industry.

title: A. O. Smith launches CO₂ split heat pump water heater for residential use
content:
A. O. Smith has launched the Voltex X, an outdoor split-system heat pump water heater using CO₂ refrigerant and designed for cold-climate operation down to -31.7 C. The system offers up to 303 L of storage, smart controls, leak and freeze protection, and a 10-year limited warranty.

title: Perovskite solar tested at over 5,000 m altitude
content:
Monochrome will test a perovskite PV prototype at an altitude of around 5,150 meters during an alpine expedition in Pakistan's Karakoram region. The field trial will assess power-generation performance and durability under harsh, off-grid conditions as the company explores perovskite technology for future BIPV applications.

title: European Patent Office revokes Hanwha’s long-disputed passivation patent
content:
The European Patent Office has revoked Hanwha Solutions’ 689 patent covering passivation technology used in silicon solar cells, citing a lack of inventive step. The decision follows years of patent litigation between Hanwha Q Cells and solar manufacturers including JinkoSolar, Longi and REC across Europe, the US and Australia.

title: Researchers near 100% silver recovery from end-of-life solar panels
content:
Researchers at the University of Newcastle have achieved almost 100% silver recovery from end-of-life solar panels using a proven mineral-processing technology they believe could make solar panel recycling more economically viable.

title: Ireland’s leap of faith to power data centers
content:
Under Ireland’s Large Energy User Action Plan (LEAP), 10 MW-plus data centers must provide at least 80% of their energy demand through new onsite renewable energy generation and storage. But whether data centers can meaningfully contribute to Ireland’s decarbonization depends on the success of its grid buildout, reports Blathnaid O’Dea.
